body: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed with hierarchical instructions, yet they remain vulnerable to conflicts in which user directives override system-level constraints. Existing defense mechanisms predominantly focus on static input inspection and therefore fail to detect Response Drift, a phenomenon in which the model's final response violates system-level constraints despite seemingly compliant inputs. To bridge this gap, we introduce ELCD, a response-level latent conflict detector for post-generation, pre-delivery verification. Given the full generated output, ELCD constructs a composite hidden-state representation by concatenating the final-token embedding with the mean-pooled response embedding. It then optimizes a pairwise margin ranking objective to separate compliant and drifting responses in latent space. Extensive experiments across five mainstream LLMs ranging from 1.5B to 14B parameters demonstrate that ELCD significantly outperforms competitive baselines. Notably, it improves the PR-AUC on Llama-2-7B by approximately 30 percentage points and reduces the False Positive Rate at 95% TPR (FPR95) on Mistral-7B to 2.67%. These results suggest that ELCD provides a promising approach for latent instruction-conflict detection in open-weight or self-hosted LLM deployments.
summaryZh: 针对大语言模型（LLM）在执行层级指令时可能出现的指令冲突（用户指令覆盖系统约束）问题，该研究提出了一种名为ELCD（Energy-Driven Latent Conflict Detection）的响应级潜在冲突检测方法。ELCD在模型生成响应后、交付前进行验证，通过构建复合隐藏状态表示并优化排序目标，实现在潜在空间中区分合规响应与冲突响应。实验表明，ELCD在多个主流LLM上显著优于现有基线方法，能大幅提高PR-AUC并降低误报率，为开放权重或自托管LLM的部署提供了有效的安全保障。
